doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Studio work, Rudy Van Gelder and Freddie Hubbard
title: Creed Taylor's confrontation with Bill Evans on tour
summary: Laws recalls Creed Taylor and saxophonist Bill Evans having a heated exchange on the recent European CTI tour.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Did most musicians understand and appreciate his vision? Or did you see any kind of conflict? Well, you already described him as a person who had a mediator come in. So I guess that’s the way he dealt with it. Because, you know, musicians can be very opinionated.

Except for that time when he dealt with Bill Evans on this tour. They actually had a little bit of an abrasive conversation in there, and that was mainly because of Bill. He’s kind of an energetic and in-your-face type guy. At least he was then. That’s the first time I actually met Bill. I didn’t even know about Bill Evans, the saxophone player. I knew about the piano player. That was it. But I never had heard of him. He had a career that eluded me. When he confronted Creed, that was the first time I ever saw Creed directly – but it wasn’t fiery. It was just that he said he was sticking to his guns about what he thought should be – the music should be like. He was trying to protect his image too, because this was coming out on CTI Records. They were going to record this stuff. They were recording that stuff.
He had a superlative record, known for a sound, that CTI sound.
Which I feel that Bill should have respected.
Right. Well, he was young. Maybe it was the ignorance of youth.
Bill must be in his 40s, though.
It was about two years ago.
Okay, I thought this might have been . . .
No, two years ago, when we were on tour.
. . . coming out of the Miles [Davis] band or something, having a big hit.
No, this is about two years ago. We were on tour, CTI tour, the only tour we did in Europe.
